1. The `cvt` (data conversion) instruction with `.tf32` destination type: What rounding modifiers are allowed and what do they mean? Specifically:
   - `cvt.rn.tf32.f32` — what does `.rn` mean? (round to nearest even?)
   - `cvt.rna.tf32.f32` — what does `.rna` mean? (round to nearest, ties away from zero?)
   - Is `.rz` (round toward zero / truncate) allowed for tf32?
   - Is there a DEFAULT rounding if no modifier is given for `cvt.*.tf32.f32`?
   - Quote the PTX ISA "Data Movement and Conversion Instructions: cvt" section text about tf32 rounding. Note which PTX ISA version / CUDA version introduced cvt.rn.tf32.f32 vs cvt.rna.tf32.f32.

2. The `mma` / `wgmma` / matrix-multiply-accumulate instructions with `.tf32` operand type (e.g. `mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k8.row.col.f32.tf32.tf32.f32`, and `wgmma.mma_async....tf32`): 
   - When you feed these instructions operands declared as `.tf32`, does the PTX ISA say the registers must ALREADY be in tf32 format (i.e. the programmer is responsible for converting f32->tf32 first), or does the MMA instruction itself accept full f32 and convert internally?
   - Critically: does the PTX ISA specify any ROUNDING MODE for how f32 mantissa bits beyond tf32's 10 are handled by the tensor-core MMA? Or does it say the low mantissa bits are simply IGNORED / the value is interpreted as tf32 by reading only the high bits (i.e. truncation)?
   - Quote the relevant "Warp Level Matrix Multiply-Accumulate Instructions" section text describing the tf32 data format and what happens to the extra precision. Look for language like "the low-order mantissa bits are ignored" or "rounded".

3. From the PTX ISA's description of the TF32 numeric format itself: how many mantissa bits (should be 10 explicit), exponent bits (8), and does the ISA say anything about how an f32 value is reduced to tf32 inside tensor-core ops (truncation vs rounding)?

Please give me direct quotes with the PTX ISA section numbers/titles and the URL of each page you fetched. Be precise about the distinction between the explicit `cvt` instruction's rounding (which is programmer-selected) versus the implicit conversion the tensor core does when handed f32 register data. If the docs say the MMA reads only the upper bits / truncates, state that explicitly with the quote.

# TF32 Rounding in the NVIDIA PTX ISA — Authoritative Answer

**Primary source:** *Parallel Thread Execution ISA, Release 8.7* (NVIDIA, Feb 27, 2025) — the current published PTX ISA reference.
**PDF fetched:** `https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/pdf/ptx_isa_8.7.pdf`
**HTML equivalent (single-page):** `https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/index.html`

A note on method: the official HTML is one giant single page with fragment anchors, so per-section web extraction fails; I worked from the official PDF (identical normative text). Section numbers below are from that document.

---

## 1. The `cvt` instruction with `.tf32` destination (explicit, programmer-selected rounding)

**Section 9.7.9.21 — "Data Movement and Conversion Instructions: `cvt`"**

The syntax block lists exactly two allowed forms for a `.tf32` destination:

> ```
> cvt.rna{.satfinite}.tf32.f32                    d, a;
> cvt.frnd2{.satfinite}{.relu}.tf32.f32           d, a;
> ```
> …
> ```
> .frnd2   = { .rn, .rz };
> ```

So the allowed rounding modifiers for `cvt.*.tf32.f32` are **`.rna`, `.rn`, and `.rz`** (the `.frnd2` set expands to `.rn` and `.rz`).

**Meanings** — from **Section 6.5.2, "Rounding Modifiers," Table 17 (Floating-Point Rounding Modifiers)**, and restated in the cvt section's "Floating Point Notes":

> `.rn`  rounding to nearest, with ties to even
> `.rna` rounding to nearest, with ties away from zero
> `.rz`  rounding toward zero
> `.rm`  rounding toward negative infinity
> `.rp`  rounding toward positive infinity

(Table 17 phrases these as "mantissa LSB rounds to nearest even", "…to nearest, ties away from zero", "…towards zero", etc.)

Answering your specific points:
- **`cvt.rn.tf32.f32`** → `.rn` = **round to nearest, ties to even**. ✅ (allowed)
- **`cvt.rna.tf32.f32`** → `.rna` = **round to nearest, ties away from zero**. ✅ (allowed)
- **Is `.rz` allowed for tf32?** → **Yes.** `.frnd2 = { .rn, .rz }`, so `cvt.rz.tf32.f32` is legal (round toward zero / truncate).
- **Is there a DEFAULT rounding for `cvt.*.tf32.f32`?** → **No — a rounding modifier is mandatory.** The cvt "Description" states:
  > "Rounding modifier is mandatory in all of the following cases: … ▶ All conversions involving `.f16x2`, `.e4m3x2`, `.e5m2x2`, `.bf16x2`, **`.tf32`**, `.e2m1x2`, … instruction types."

  You must write one of `.rn`, `.rna`, or `.rz` explicitly.

**Version history** (from the cvt section's "PTX ISA Notes"):
> - ".relu modifier and {.f16x2, .bf16, .bf16x2, **.tf32**} destination formats introduced in PTX ISA version 7.0."
> - "… and **`cvt.tf32.f32.{relu}.{rn∕rz}`** introduced in PTX ISA 7.8." (Target-ISA note: requires sm_90 or higher.)
> - "`cvt.satfinite.{f16, bf16, f16x2, bf16x2, tf32}.f32` introduced in PTX ISA version 8.1."
> - "`cvt.{rn∕rz}.satfinite.tf32.f32` introduced in PTX ISA version 8.6." (requires sm_100 or higher.)

So the `.rn`/`.rz` forms for tf32 arrived in **PTX ISA 7.8 / CUDA 11.8 (sm_90+)**, while the `.tf32` destination itself (the canonical fp32→tf32 conversion) dates to **PTX ISA 7.0 (CUDA 11.0, sm_80+)**.

Important nuance on **`.rna`**: the document does **not** give `.rna.tf32.f32` an explicit "introduced in version X" line, but the syntax block lists `cvt.rna{.satfinite}.tf32.f32` as a first-class form, and the comment examples use it (line ref below). `.rna` (round-to-nearest, ties-away) is the rounding mode that matches the hardware tensor-core behavior and is the conversion `__float_to_tf32`-style helpers and `cvt.rna.tf32.f32` emit. The example block in the cvt section shows:

> ```
> cvt.rna.satfinite.tf32.f32   b1, f;   // convert fp32 to tf32 format
> cvt.rn.relu.tf32.f32         d, a;    // convert fp32 to tf32 format
> cvt.rn.satfinite.tf32.f32    d, a;    // convert fp32 to tf32 format

## 2. The `mma` / `wmma` / `wgmma` instructions with `.tf32` operands (implicit reduction inside the tensor core)

**Section 9.7.14 / 9.7.15 — "Warp Level Matrix Multiply-Accumulate Instructions"** and its subsections.

### Do the registers have to be in tf32 format already? → YES. The programmer converts first.

Two pieces of normative text establish this:

1. **The format definition (Section 5.2.x, "Alternate Floating-Point Data Formats" / the `tf32 data format` entry):**
   > "tf32 data format: This data format is a special 32-bit floating point format supported by the matrix multiply-and-accumulate instructions, with the same range as `.f32` and reduced precision (>=10 bits). The internal layout of tf32 format is implementation defined. **PTX facilitates conversion from single precision `.f32` type to tf32 format. A register variable containing tf32 data must be declared with `.b32` type.**"

2. **The MMA fragment tables** declare tf32 multiplicand fragments as raw `.b32` registers, not `.f32`:
   > "Floating point fragments for `.tf32` data format — Multiplicands (A or B): `.tf32` … A vector expression of four **`.b32`** registers."

So the operand registers hold an already-converted, opaque 32-bit tf32 bit pattern (`.b32`). The programmer is responsible for the f32→tf32 conversion (typically via `cvt.rn.tf32.f32` / `cvt.rna.tf32.f32`, or `wmma.load … .tf32` which loads tf32-formatted data). The MMA instruction consumes tf32, it does **not** advertise an internal f32→tf32 step.

### Does the ISA specify a ROUNDING MODE for how f32 mantissa bits beyond tf32's 10 are handled by the MMA? → NO.

This is the precise, citable negative result, and it is unambiguous:

- The `wmma.mma` / `mma.sync` syntax for tf32 has **no `.rnd` / rounding qualifier at all**. Compare the two adjacent forms in the wmma section:
  > ```
  > Floating point format .tf32 wmma.mma:
  > wmma.mma.sync.aligned.alayout.blayout.shape.f32.atype.btype.f32 d, a, b, c;
  > .atype = {.tf32 };  .btype = {.tf32};        // <-- NO .rnd
  >
  > Floating point Double precision wmma.mma:
  > wmma.mma.sync.aligned.alayout.blayout.shape{.rnd}.f64.f64.f64.f64 d, a, b, c;
  > .rnd = { .rn, .rz, .rm, .rp };                // <-- .f64 DOES have .rnd
  > ```
  The `.f64` MMA explicitly exposes a rounding mode; the `.tf32` MMA does not. The tf32 inputs are already tf32 (`.b32`), so there is no rounding decision for the instruction to expose at its input.

- I searched the **entire** ISA text for any such language in the MMA/wmma/wgmma sections — there is **no** statement like "the low-order mantissa bits are ignored," "truncated," or "rounded" anywhere in the warp-level / warpgroup MMA descriptions. The only occurrences of "mantissa," "rounded," "truncated," or "ignored" in a precision sense are in (a) the **`cvt`** instruction, (b) the scalar arithmetic instructions (`add`/`mul`/`fma`/`mad`), and (c) the format-bit-count definitions — none in the MMA operation semantics.

**Conclusion for the MMA path:** The PTX ISA does **not** define a rounding mode for an implicit f32→tf32 conversion inside the tensor core, because at the PTX level there is no implicit conversion — the operands are required to already be tf32 (`.b32`). Any reduction of full f32 precision to tf32 must be done *beforehand* with `cvt` (where rounding is programmer-selected, normally `.rna`). The internal tf32 layout itself is declared **"implementation defined,"** so the bit-level handling of mantissa beyond 10 bits is left unspecified by PTX rather than defined as truncation-vs-rounding.

(For completeness: the one place the ISA says fp32 is "rounded to nearest even" toward tf32 is **not** an MMA statement — it is the **TMA / tensor copy** path, Section 5.5.1: "Floating point and alternate floating point: `.f16, .bf16, .tf32, .f32, .f64` (rounded to nearest even)." That governs `cp`/tensor loads, not the MMA arithmetic.)

## 3. The TF32 numeric format itself

**Section 5.2.x, `tf32 data format` (quoted in full in §2 above):**
- **Mantissa bits:** the ISA states "reduced precision (**>=10 bits**)" — i.e., *at least* 10 mantissa bits, not pinned to exactly 10. (By contrast the `.f16` entry pins "10 bits reserved for mantissa," and `.bf16` "7 bits for mantissa." TF32 is deliberately specified as a lower bound, ">=10".)
- **Exponent bits:** the ISA says tf32 has "the same range as `.f32`," and `.f32` has an 8-bit exponent — so **8 exponent bits** (matching bf16's "8 bits for exponent"). The ISA does not separately print "8 bits for exponent" for tf32; it expresses it as "same range as `.f32`."
- **How f32 is reduced to tf32 inside tensor-core ops:** the ISA does **not** specify this as truncation-vs-rounding. It says only that the **"internal layout of tf32 format is implementation defined,"** and that **"PTX facilitates conversion from single precision `.f32` type to tf32 format"** — i.e., the conversion is a separate, explicit `cvt` step whose rounding the programmer selects (`.rn`/`.rna`/`.rz`); it is not a property of the MMA instruction.

## Bottom line (the distinction you asked me to be precise about)

| | Explicit `cvt.*.tf32.f32` | Implicit reduction inside MMA |
|---|---|---|
| Rounding specified by ISA? | **Yes, mandatory & programmer-selected:** `.rn` (nearest-even), `.rna` (nearest-ties-away), or `.rz` (toward zero). No default. | **No.** No rounding qualifier exists on the tf32 MMA form; operands must already be tf32 (`.b32`). |
| Does it truncate / "read only high bits"? | Only if you pick `.rz`. | The ISA makes **no truncation/rounding claim** for MMA; it requires pre-converted tf32 input and calls the internal layout "implementation defined." |

The PTX ISA does **not** state "the MMA reads only the upper bits / truncates." It instead requires the operand to already be tf32 (`.b32`) and leaves the format's internal layout implementation-defined; the precision reduction is the programmer's explicit `cvt` (normally `cvt.rna.tf32.f32`).
